correctness.rationale: Total domination on a complete multipartite graph is equivalent to positive support meeting at least two parts. With at least three represented parts, moving one unit from any adjacent positive donor to a zero vertex can remove at most one represented part while preserving at least two. With exactly two represented parts, a zero in \(X_i\) is protected precisely when \(X_i\) has no zero or the donor side \(X_j\) retains positive weight after a unit transfer, equivalently \(p_i=n_i\) or \(s_j\ge2\); the symmetric condition gives the criterion. The enumerator follows by subtracting one-part support and then the two bad two-part events, whose intersection is exactly the two weight-one non-full supports. The minimum-weight cases then follow by exhausting weights two, three and four. The actual verifier blob was inspected: it tests the definition vertex-by-vertex and donor-by-donor, the criterion, every enumerator coefficient, and the minimum formulas for every multipartite isomorphism type of orders two through nine.

value.rationale: Total weak Roman domination is an established graph-protection invariant. A closed all-function classification and weight enumerator on arbitrary complete multipartite graphs strictly refines the usual minimum-number results and gives exact counts at every weight, making it a natural reusable structural result.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), \(r\ge2\), a \(\{0,1,2\}\)-labeling is total weak Roman exactly when its positive support meets at least three parts, or it meets exactly two parts \(X_i,X_j\) and \((p_i=n_i\text{ or }s_j\ge2)\) and \((p_j=n_j\text{ or }s_i\ge2)\). This yields the stated closed weight enumerator for all total weak Roman functions and the stated exact minimum weights and minimum-function counts.
limitations: Finite connected complete multipartite graphs only.
